title: Why Climb Mount Meru Before Kilimanjaro
excerpt: Climbing Mount Meru before Kilimanjaro helps your body adapt to altitude and gives you a preview of summit night. Here is how to plan it.
body:
If you have a few extra days, climbing Mount Meru before Kilimanjaro is one of the smartest things you can do.

## Acclimatisation

Spending several nights between 2,500 and 3,600 m and reaching 4,566 m on Meru gives your body a head start. When you start Kilimanjaro a day or two later, you are already partly adapted.

## A rehearsal

Meru gives you a taste of a night ascent, cold temperatures and walking with a guide. You learn how your body reacts and which clothes and snacks work for you.

## How to plan it

- Day 1–4: Mount Meru (four days).
- Day 5: rest day in Arusha or Moshi.
- Day 6–12/13: Kilimanjaro, for example [Lemosho](/blog/kilimanjaro-lemosho-route-guide/) or [Machame](/blog/kilimanjaro-machame-route-guide/).

With Meru beforehand, a shorter Kilimanjaro programme becomes more manageable, but we still recommend at least seven days.

## Is it too much?

Two climbs in two weeks is demanding. It suits people who love walking and have a good base fitness. If you prefer a lighter option, a [day hike on Kilimanjaro](/blog/kilimanjaro-day-hike/) or a few days in [Arusha National Park](/national-parks/arusha-national-park/) also help.

## Also beautiful on its own

Even without Kilimanjaro, Meru is a great short climb. See our [Mount Meru guide](/blog/mount-meru-climb-guide/) and [plan your trip](/travel-proposal/).
